messages:
incident-bot: PAGE fired — p99 latency breach for inference-frontend (eu-west) 

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert: PD-56321 triggered (p99 > 3s over 5m). Escalation to on-call. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-56321

maya: ack'd. I'm on it. 

toni: pulling metrics now, seeing p95 ~ 1.1s but p99 spike to ~3.6s, starts ~14:02 UTC. CPU/GPU don't look saturated. Sidecars show increased queue waits. 

sam-ops: confirm, tail logs from frontend show long wait at model-req-queue: "enqueue_time_ms" ~ 1200-2500 for many shards. Might be KV-cache miss storms? 

alex: any recent rollout in eu-west? model-v2.3 rolled yesterday night to 40% traffic. Could be cold KV layout. 

maya: yes, v2.3 40% ramp. It uses new attention-kernel drop-in. 

toni: running quick heatmap of KV cache hit-rate per pod... one AZ (eu-west-1b) has hit-rate drop to 18% while others at 85%. That could cause long tail due to remote fetch. 

maya: good catch — if one AZ's cache warmed poorly, that explains burst. Options: 1) reroute traffic off that AZ, 2) roll model back to v2.2 for canary traffic, 3) force cache warm/warmup script. 

alex: can we quick-canary rollback v2.3 -> v2.2 for canary 40%? That should reduce variance. I can flip routing if ops approves. 

sam-ops: i can reroute canary traffic immediately to v2.2 in eu-west. Doing safe swap for 40% now. 

sam-ops: (command) ```
redwood route update inference-frontend --region eu-west --model v2.2 --traffic 40
```

sam-ops: route change submitted. PD note: manual rollback initiated by sam-ops. 

toni: verifying pods... looks like canary pods switched to v2.2. Starting to see p99 fall in one shard already from 3.6s -> 2.0s. 

maya: pushing a quick health-check script to force warmups on the bad AZ: ```for i in {1..50}; do curl -s "https://inference-eu-west.internal/health?model=v2.2" >/dev/null; sleep 0.2; done``` doing warmup now in parallel across pods. 

incident-bot: Note: 1779004321 — manual mitigation action logged: rollback-canary + cache-warmup 

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty update: incident acknowledged by maya; assignee: oncall-sre (maya). 

alex: metrics after 3m: p99 1.4s, p95 0.9s. KV miss-rate dropping. Looks promising. 

toni: still watching, but tail latency spike count down 85%. No customer-facing errors reported in support queue yet. 

maya: reached out to support to confirm impact: @support please flag any customers experiencing slow responses. 

sam-ops: support reply: "small uptick in latency reported by two customers in EU, not widespread, no errors." 

maya: that's consistent with partial AZ/route impact. Let's keep canary rolled back for now and continue warmup for 20m. 

toni: agree. I'll leave autoscaler alone; no scaling triggers necessary. Will set an alert suppression window in PagerDuty to avoid noisy autopages while we stabilize. 

pagerduty-bot: Suppression window requested by toni for PD-56321: 20m (reason: manual mitigation in progress). 

alex: quick postmortem notes: likely cause = v2.3 canary + uneven KV cache distribution on AZ-1 leading to remote fetch tail. Action items: (A) full rollback of v2.3 canary until cache warm strategy in place, (B) improve cache warmup during deploys, (C) add per-AZ KV-hit-rate alert. 

maya: creating incident ticket now and assigning owners. Ticket: INC-2026-0456 created. Severity: P2. Owners: toni, alex. ETA for full writeup by EOD. 

sam-ops: removing suppression in 18m if stable. 

toni: p99 holding ~1.2s for last 4m, no new PD alerts. I'm going to mark the incident as mitigated in channel in 10m if it stays steady. 

maya: thanks everyone. Quick handoff to oncall rotation: @alex will be backup from 15:00-18:00 UTC. I'll stay as incident lead until EOD. 

alex: ack, standing by. :thumbsup: 

incident-bot: UPDATE: PD-56321 mitigated metrics OK for 12m. No active pages. 

maya: marking thread resolved for now. I'll attach logs and timeline to the ticket, and schedule postmortem writeup with toni/alex.

sam-ops: noted. leaving route rolled back to v2.2 for all canary traffic in eu-west until we have warmup + perf signoff. 

maya: follow-ups: add cache-warmup to rollout playbook, run a canary soak for 60m next deploy, per-AZ KV hit-rate alerts. Assigning to toni (runbook) and alex (deploy changes).

toni: will draft runbook edits and alert rules. 

alex: will add warmup hooks to our CI deploy job. 

maya: closing incident thread — filing postmortem, pinging eng-docs to link. Thanks team. :heart:
